title: Watchlist sync and rollout forecast (Apr 2026) - notes
summary: Working notes for synchronizing the stability watchlist with observability teams and a compact rollout forecast for the next sprint. Focus: sampling windows, alert thresholds, operator handoffs, and rapid rollback triggers. Intended as an ops checklist + rough release notes draft to push to stakeholders for early review.
checklist: Confirm final canary traffic bucket sizes (0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50%)
Ensure telemetry sampling increases for model-routing signals during 2% and 10% phases
Instrument the KV-cache warmup metric in the runtime (obs: kv_cache_hit_ratio) and add to watchlist
Pre-deploy fallback model variant to the standby pool and test endpoint failover
Update PagerDuty routing for 'latency-regression' to include serving-runtime on-call (primary + secondary)
Coordinate reduced alert noise window (quiet-window) from 02:00–05:00 UTC for initial canary burst
Create smoke test job that runs in prod staging canary every 5m for first 4 hours of each phase
Lock feature flags for rollout gating and ensure override is gated to SRE leads only
Send the pre-launch brief to PM/Docs/Support and schedule 30m sync at T-24h
rollout_calendar:
2026-04-18 08:00 UTC - Cutover start: push model v2.1 image to canary pool (0.5%).
2026-04-18 09:30 UTC - Observe 90m: check latency, error-rate, kv_cache_hit_ratio, mem spikes.
2026-04-18 11:00 UTC - Expand to 2% for 3h; enable extended sampling and full tracing for a subset of requests.
2026-04-18 14:30 UTC - Decision point: if SLOs within tolerance = progress to 10%, else rollback to v2.0 and escalate.
2026-04-18 18:00 UTC - 10% sustained for 6h with automated throttles active; begin 50% ramp if stable.
2026-04-19 02:00 UTC - Final assessment and ramp to 100% or rollforward maintained with staggered regional backfills.
Notes: local timeframes for NA/EU/APAC staggered by 4–6h windows; operator rotation 4h-slots during ramp hours.
release_notes_draft: Release v2.1 (runtime + model): main changes: optimized KV cache usage for longer context windows, improved attention kernel selection for mixed-precision quantized checkpoints, and minor API contract stabilization for streaming chunks. Expected user impact: lower token latency tail by ~10–20% on medium-length requests; no breaking changes for existing clients. Known issues: occasional cold-start latency on new dedicated nodes (workaround: pre-warm nodes via deployment job). Rollout strategy: staged canary -> regional ramp -> full rollforward with automatic fallbacks. If customers observe increased 5xx rates, toggle 'serving.experimental.fallback' to true and contact SRE.
